newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Local trader supports market.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Local trader supports market.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices were well supported on Tuesday as recent demand from a local trader continued, traders said.
No deals were heard done by late Tuesday but traders said they expected a slight upward trend this week.
The Singapore-based trader, who said the company was seeking to cover its short positions, has bought at least two cargoes last week and one cargo on Monday.
Its sister company bought one cargo last week.

Some traders said the Singapore trader was buying the cargoes to supply Indonesia, whose state oil firm Pertamina is expected to shut down some units in the 200,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Balikpapan refinery for maintenance from July 10 for 32 days.
"The trader is buying for July cargoes, which is very likely for Indonesia's maintenance shutdown," said one trader.
The Singapore trader bought a 180-cst cargo for July 19-23 lifting at $101.50 per tonne on Monday. It bid on Tuesday at $100.00, but failed to attract any sellers.
Traders said majors were unwilling to sell at the lower level, believing the Singapore trader would bid up the market in coming days, traders said.

Also on Monday, the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organization (KEDO) bought 36,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil from British Petroleum's BP.L BP Singapore Pte Ltd and up to 24,000 tonnes from Mitsubishi Corp's 8058.T Petro Diamond Co Ltd for July delivery.
BP sold the oil for $120.90 per tonne for delivery to Sonbong, North Korea in one cargo during July 21-30.
Petro Diamond sold 22,000 to 24,000 tonnes loading in Aichi, Japan during July 15-19 at $109.75 per tonne, with freight to Nampo and Songrim, North Korea, at $18.75 per tonne.
On the supply side, Taiwan's state Chinese Petroleum Corp will close a term tender on Wednesday to sell six 30,000-tonne cargoes of 3.0-percent fuel oil.
Fuel oil swaps edged up also over physical market demand, traders said.
July swaps were at $99.50/$100.50 against $98.25/$100.00 and August were at $98.75/$99.50 against $98.25/$99.00.
In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, traders were waiting for the July LSWR allocation details from Indonesia's Pertamina.
Traders said Pertamina was likely to decrease its July allocation to lower than 2.5 million barrels, compared with 3.6 million barrels in June, due to the Balikpapan maintenance shutdown.
"If the low allocation is true, I won't be surprised that prices go up to above $16.00 or even $17.00 per barrel," said one trader.
Japanese LSWR demand for the summer is expected to emerge in late June or early July, traders said.
